llm.summary: This is an instruction-only, coherent “daily book oracle” skill that fetches a daily book from a configurable API and produces a short, optimistic reading; its needs and behavior match its description.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with actions: the skill only needs to fetch a book record and generate a short reading. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or permissions are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md confines runtime actions to calling a configured API URL, rendering the returned book metadata, generating a short fortune-style reading, and optionally showing an audio CTA or cover image. It does not instruct reading unrelated files or exfiltrating extra data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec or packaged code—this is instruction-only. INSTALL.md suggests use of platform commands (clawhub/openclaw) to enable scheduled pushes; those are platform-native and expected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables or credentials are declared. Optional config keys (API URL, audio base, language, show audio) are reasonable for this feature and proportional to the skill's purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation are used. The INSTALL.md describes adding a scheduled cron push via the platform (expected behavior); the skill does not request elevated or persistent platform-wide privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is low-risk and internally consistent, but note: it fetches book data from an external API (default: https://book-of-the-day.vercel.app). If you care about privacy or want control over the data source, set BOOK_OF_THE_DAY_API_URL to a self-hosted endpoint or verify the publisher's API. The INSTALL.md recommends running platform install/schedule commands—only run those if you trust the skill source and understand that scheduled pushes will post messages to your configured channels. Finally, one-command installers can write to your OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) to store the API URL — review that file and its permissions after setup.
